You are given 20 mL of a sample solution which is created by dissolving an unknown, pure inorganic salt in distilled water. The salt consists of one type of cation and one type of anion. Your task is to perform tests and experiments on the sample using the given tools and reagents, and use the resulting observations to deduce the identity of the unknown salt. Most experiments will consume a portion of the involved solutions, including the unknown sample. If you run out of the sample, you cannot perform any tests that use it but you can keep experimenting with other solutions in the Inventory from the previously performed tests. NOTE: All solutions are at room temperature.

<thought>
Perfect! A black precipitate forms when AgNO3 is added to the sample. This is consistent with Ag2O (silver oxide), which forms when Ag+ reacts with OH-:

2Ag+ + 2OH- → Ag2O(s) + H2O

The black precipitate confirms the presence of OH- anion.

Let me also verify there are no other anions present by testing for common anions:
- Halides (Cl-, Br-, I-) would form white/cream/yellow precipitates with Ag+
- Sulfate (SO4-2) would form white precipitate with Ba+2
- Phosphate (PO4-3) would form yellow precipitate with Ag+

Since we got a black precipitate (Ag2O) and not white/cream/yellow, this rules out halides and phosphates.

Let me do one more test to be sure - test with Ba(NO3)2 to rule out sulfate or phosphate:
</thought>
